content:
**Test image observations:**
- Tomato leaf with multiple small-to-medium dark brown spots scattered across the surface
- Spots have darker edges/borders, some appear to have slightly lighter centers
- No obvious concentric rings (rules out Early Blight)
- No powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)
- No webbing (rules out Spider Mites)
- No yellowing/curling (rules out TYLCV)
- No mosaic pattern (rules out viral diseases)
- Leaf otherwise green and intact

**Candidate analysis:**
- **Bacterial_Spot**: Small dark brown circular lesions, some with centers that may drop out (shot-hole), scattered pattern — matches well
- **Septoria_Leaf_Spot**: Small lesions with tan/gray centers, dark perimeter, pycnidia — possible, but centers here look darker not tan
- **Target_Spot**: Concentric rings with light centers — reference shows mostly subtle small spots, but the test spots lack the ring pattern

The spots in the test image are small, dark brown, scattered without distinct concentric rings or a tan/gray center typical of Septoria. The dark lesions with no clear halos and slightly irregular shape best match **Bacterial_Spot**.
